newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Indian Hutti gold to set up j.v. exploration firms.
newsitem.headline: Indian Hutti gold to set up j.v. exploration firms.

text.p: India's Hutti Gold Mine Co Ltd is negotiating with Australian companies to form joint venture gold exploration firms to exploit India's vast potential gold deposits, chairman K.N. Shrivastava said on Tuesday.
"We are in talks with a number of companies, including RTZ-CRA, Broken Hill Proprietary and Western Mining Corporation," he said.
"We hope to finalise some joint ventures within three months," Shrivastava, who is also managing director of the company, told Reuters.
A government announcement on India's gold exploration policy is expected by mid-October, he said.
The policy would allow foreign companies to take more than 50 percent equity in gold exploration joint ventures, he said.
"The policy is being reviewed and formulated to promote a congenial environment where joint venture projects can take up exploration and embark on exploitation of potential gold deposits," he said.
Shrivastava is in Hong Kong to attend a three-day Asian Gold Congress.
He said India's state and federal governments were aware that mining exploration projects, which are both capital and technology intensive, were beyond their means without foreign participation.
After India repealed its Gold Control Act in 1990, artificially high domestic prices began to more closely reflect international levels, he said.
When prices dropped, local gold companies "started to feel the pinch," he said.
Hutti also has plans for expanding production and mechanisation at its mine in Karnataka state, worth US$30 million, he said.
There were 80 confirmed gold deposits in the southern Indian state, and although they appeared small, further exploration could reveal substantial potential, he said.

To boost production and maintain profitability, Hutti would expand gold production to three tonnes a year, from one tonne now, at Kanartika by modernising and mechanising the mine and expanding the metallurgical plant to mine and mill 3,000 tonnes per day of gold ore.
Demand for gold in India increased in 1995 to a record 474 tonnes, compared with the previous high of 454 tonnes in 1992, Indian media reported earlier this year.
Demand in 1996 was expected to hit 500 tonnes, the Economic Times said, with 8,000 to 10,000 tonnes believed to be hoarded in the country.
The paper said India produced a mere two tonnes of gold a year despite being one of the largest gold markets, accounting for around 10 percent of world demand.
